title: Quasi-finite affine decomposition after a surjective base change
statement: Let $h:V\to U$ be a quasi-finite morphism [pqf-def-quasifinite] of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]). There exist an affine scheme $U\prime$, a surjective morphism $a:U\prime\to U$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow V\prime=V\times_U U\prime$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product] which is surjective on underlying points (a thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]), such that the composite $Z\xrightarrow{i}V\prime\to U\prime$ is finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category].

proof.text: Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The affine-open finite-presentation theorem, applied to the whole source and target as affine opens, makes $B$ a finitely presented $A$-algebra. Index the finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras of $A$ by inclusion; their union is $A$, and the union has the ring-colimit universal property since a compatible family of ring maps is defined element by element. The index is a small nonempty directed set: adjoining the union of two finite generating sets gives an upper bound. Apply finite-presentation descent to obtain $B_0$ finitely presented over some $A_0$, with $B\cong A\otimes_{A_0}B_0$. The affine quasi-finiteness descent lemma gives a later stage $A_i\to B_i$ which is quasi-finite. Put $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ and $h_0:V_0\to U_0$. Both schemes are of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and hence Noetherian by the cited theorem. The affine fibre-product formula identifies $h$ with the pullback of $h_0$ along $U\to U_0$. We construct the required cover for $h_0$ in steps 2-9, then pull it back in step 10.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: We partition $U_0$ so that $h_0$ becomes finite on each piece. Explicitly, for each reduced closed subscheme $T\subseteq U_0$, apply the locally-quasi-finite base-change lemma and quasi-compact base change to $V_0\times_{U_0}T\to T$. The locally-quasi-finite plus quasi-compact criterion gives quasi-finiteness; the finite-fibres criterion then gives finite fibres and local finite type. This morphism is between affine schemes, hence quasi-separated (its diagonal is induced by the surjection $C\otimes_D C\to C$), and is locally of finite type as just established. The generic-finiteness theorem therefore supplies a dense open $O\subseteq T$ where it is finite. A closed subscheme of the Noetherian affine $U_0$ is Noetherian: its coordinate ring is a quotient, and every quotient ideal is generated by the images of finitely many generators of its inverse image. Take its reduced structure for $T$; the same argument applies. Partition $O$ by reduced locally closed affine subschemes using the affine-partition lemma. Finiteness persists on a piece $S$: as $O$ need not be affine, cover it by standard opens $D_T(g)$ of $T$; over each, $h_0$ is finite (restriction clause of the finite-locality theorem), hence so is its base change to $D_S(g)=S\cap D_T(g)$, since $1\otimes c_1,\ldots,1\otimes c_r$ generate a tensor base change of a module generated by $c_1,\ldots,c_r$; these $D_S(g)$ cover $S$, so the same theorem makes the pullback to $S$ finite. Repeat on the reduced closed complement $T\setminus O$. The underlying space of $U_0$ is Noetherian by the affine Noetherian-space lemma, so this strict descending chain of closed complements terminates. Beginning with $T=(U_0)_{\mathrm{red}}$ yields finitely many reduced locally closed affine strata $S_t\to U_0$ covering all its points, and $Y_t=V_0\times_{U_0}S_t\to S_t$ is finite. The empty complement is the terminal case.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: For each finite affine map $Y_t\to S_t$, apply the section-cover lemma. It gives a surjective finite locally free $A_t\to S_t$, a closed immersion $Y_t\times_{S_t}A_t\hookrightarrow W_t$, and finitely many closed sections $s_k:A_t\cong W_{t,k}\subseteq W_t$ covering the underlying space of $W_t$. The scheme $A_t$ is affine and Noetherian: a finite algebra is of finite type (module generators also generate it as an algebra), so finite-type preservation of Noetherianity applies to $A_t\to S_t$. Here $S_t$ is Noetherian: it is a closed subscheme of an open subscheme of the Noetherian $T$ of step 2, hence locally Noetherian (opens of locally Noetherian schemes are locally Noetherian, quotients of Noetherian rings are Noetherian), and affine, hence quasi-compact. Set $Y_{A_t}=Y_t\times_{S_t}A_t$.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: In $A_t$, let $C_k=s_k^{-1}(Y_{A_t})$. Let $D_{k\ell}$ be the equalizer of $s_k,s_\ell:A_t\to W_t$, defined as the pullback of the diagonal $W_t\to W_t\times_{A_t}W_t$. The diagonal is a closed immersion: for affine coordinates $A_t=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and $W_t=\operatorname{Spec}C$, its ring map is the surjective multiplication $C\otimes_D C\to C$. Closed-immersion base change therefore makes both $C_k$ and $D_{k\ell}$ closed subschemes of $A_t$. Apply the Boolean affine refinement lemma to this finite family on the Noetherian affine $A_t$. It gives a finite partition by reduced locally closed affine schemes $R$ on which each pulled-back $C_k$ and $D_{k\ell}$ has either no points or all points of $R$.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: Fix one such $R$. The closed sections still cover $W_R=W_t\times_{A_t}R$. Indeed, write $W_t=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and let $J_k$ be the ideals of the covering closed sections. The affine fibre-product formula gives the coordinate ring $C_R$ of $W_R$. Every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $C_R$ contracts to a prime of $C$ containing some $J_k$, since the original sections cover. Hence $J_kC_R\subseteq\mathfrak q$, placing the point on the corresponding pulled-back closed section.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: On the reduced affine $R$, a pulled-back $C_k$ or $D_{k\ell}$ with all points has defining ideal $J$ with $V(J)=\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(R,\mathcal O_R)$. The reduced-ideal-intersection lemma applied to $J,J$ gives $J=J\cap J=0$. Thus this closed subscheme equals $R$ as a scheme; one with no points is empty. Accordingly every pulled-back section is either contained in $Y_R$ as a scheme or disjoint from it, and each pair either coincides as schemes or is disjoint.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: Fix one such $R$. Choose one representative of every equality class of sections that is contained in $Y_R=Y_{A_t}\times_{A_t}R$; let their number be $n_R$, which may be zero. They are pairwise disjoint closed subschemes of $Y_R$, each isomorphic to $R$, and their union contains every point of $Y_R$: the ambient sections cover all points, and a section whose inverse image of $Y_R$ is empty contributes none. Write $R=\operatorname{Spec}D$, $Y_R=\operatorname{Spec}C$, and let $I_1,\ldots,I_{n_R}$ be the ideals of these closed sections, with $C/I_j\cong D$ as $D$-algebras. Disjointness gives pairwise comaximal ideals. The Chinese remainder theorem gives $C/(\bigcap_j I_j)\cong D^{n_R}$. Consequently $E_R=\coprod_{j=1}^{n_R}R\to Y_R$ is a closed immersion by the quotient description, and is surjective on points by the covering just proved; it is a thickening. For $n_R=0$, the covering says $Y_R$ is empty, and the same assertion uses the empty scheme and the zero ring. The morphism $E_R\to R$ is etale by the coproduct-copies theorem and finite because $D^{n_R}$ is a module generated by its finitely many coordinate idempotents. This proves finite etaleness without asserting that the nonreduced $Y_R\to R$ is etale.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: Let $T_0$ be the finite coproduct of all the affine schemes $R$ obtained for every $t$, and $E_0$ the corresponding coproduct of the $E_R$. The finite affine coproduct-spectrum theorem makes $T_0$ affine, including the empty family. The composite $T_0\to U_0$ is surjective because the $S_t$ cover $U_0$, every $A_t\to S_t$ is surjective, and the $R$ cover $A_t$. Put $P_0=V_0\times_{U_0}T_0$. Its restriction over the open-and-closed component $R\subseteq T_0$ is $Y_R$, by the fibre-product universal property. The maps $E_R\to Y_R\to P_0$ assemble uniquely to $i_0:E_0\to P_0$ by the coproduct mapping property. Its inverse image over $Y_R$ is $E_R$: different base components are disjoint, while the indicated component is mapped over $R$.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: On the open cover of $P_0$ by the $Y_R$, the restrictions of $i_0$ are precisely the closed immersions $E_R\to Y_R$ of step 7. The target-locality lemma therefore makes $i_0$ a closed immersion. It is surjective on points because each restriction is, so it is a thickening. The composite $E_0\to T_0$ restricts over each open-and-closed $R$ to the finite etale morphism $E_R\to R$ of step 7. The same locality lemma, now for finiteness and etaleness, makes this composite finite etale.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof specialized to part (1)

proof.text: Finally put $U\prime=U\times_{U_0}T_0$ and $Z=U\times_{U_0}E_0$. The affine fibre-product formula makes $U\prime$ affine. Surjectivity of $T_0\to U_0$ persists under base change, so $a:U\prime\to U$ is surjective. Reassociating fibre products by their universal property identifies $V\times_U U\prime$ with the pullback of $V_0\times_{U_0}T_0$ along $U\to U_0$. The closed immersion $E_0\to V_0\times_{U_0}T_0$ stays a closed immersion and stays surjective on points by the two cited base-change lemmas. Thus its pullback $i:Z\hookrightarrow V\times_U U\prime$ is a thickening. Finite etaleness of $E_0\to T_0$ persists under the base-change functor in the finite-etale category, yielding $Z\to U\prime$ finite etale. These are exactly the clauses of the item.
